A memory-mapped control/status register block with a simple synchronous register-bus interface. Parameter ADDR_W (default 4). Ports: clk, rst_n, sel, write, addr[ADDR_W-1:0], wdata[31:0], rdata[31:0], ready, irq. A transaction occurs on a clock edge where sel is high: when write is high the addressed register is written from wdata, otherwise the addressed register's value is presented on rdata on the same edge, and ready is asserted for exactly that one cycle. Register map: address 0 is CTRL (read-write, reset 0); address 1 is STATUS (read-only to the bus; bit 0 is the sticky event flag); address 2 is EVENT_CLEAR (write-1-to-clear: writing a 1 to bit 0 clears the STATUS event flag; reads return 0); address 3 is VERSION (read-only constant 32'h0000_0001); all other addresses read as 0 and ignore writes. A separate input port event_in sets the STATUS event flag on any cycle it is high, taking priority over a simultaneous clear. The irq output is high whenever the STATUS event flag is 1 and CTRL bit 0 (interrupt enable) is 1. Reset clears CTRL and the STATUS event flag.
